scores.evidence: MVP: catalog with versioning, flat and per-seat subscriptions, the invoice state machine, the ledger, a single PSP (Stripe)
scores.rationale: Phases broadly go from core (catalog/ledger) to usage to enterprise to scale, but nothing is proven before dependents and the MVP is a lump with no substrate-first ordering or proof gates.

scores.evidence: MVP (one cell, about 3 to 4 months, small team): catalog with versioning, flat and per-seat subscriptions, the invoice state machine, the ledger, a single PSP (Stripe)
scores.rationale: The MVP is a reduced end-to-end slice, but it is 3–4 months of many features and not a thin prod walking skeleton.

scores.evidence: Decisions to make early (they're expensive to change later): Merchant of record or tenant-owned PSP accounts... Ledger-first design.
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed up front with reasons, but there are no explicit defaults or flip conditions, except partly for the database-per-tenant choice.
Nothing orders work within phases by blast radius; phases are flat lists of features.

scores.evidence: MVP: ... outbox webhooks, RLS isolation, test clocks.
scores.rationale: RLS is in the MVP and security is covered in detail in standalone sections, but later phases don't carry per-phase security work.

scores.evidence: Invariants to monitor continuously, with pages on violation: Ledger debits equal credits.
scores.rationale: Observability is a standalone section on invariants and is absent from the phase plan, including the MVP.

scores.evidence: Test clocks... Golden invoice fixtures for every pricing model, compared in CI.
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is strong in design (deterministic rating, explicit time, replayable lake), but there is no phase-tied environment or build reproducibility such as IaC.

scores.evidence: Worker crashes mid-invoice | Workflow resumes, and a unique key on (subscription, period) prevents duplicates
scores.rationale: The failure-mode table and idempotency are thorough, but they sit in a standalone section and are not tied to each phase.
The plan never states whether an AI layer applies or is N/A.

scores.evidence: Some of those answers could remove large parts of this design, such as the metering pipeline or the cells.
scores.rationale: Later phases imply deferral of usage, enterprise and scale work, but there are no explicit not-built-yet lists or pull-forward conditions.

note: The design is technically deep, but the plan is weak on delivery-process discipline: no explicit flip conditions, blast-radius ordering or per-phase threading, and the AI layer is never addressed.
